data.cultural_impact: The name Waliha holds a significant cultural impact in Islamic societies as it is often given to girls, particularly those who are expected to take on protective and nurturing roles within their families and communities. The name signifies strength, resilience, and the ability to shield and care for those around them.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Waliha lies in its connection to the role of a guardian or caretaker in Islamic theology. In Islamic tradition, the belief is that every Muslim is assigned a guardian angel, or Wali, who protects and guides them throughout their lives. The name Waliha, in a spiritual sense, can be seen as a reminder of the presence and support of God and His divine angels. It is also a call to strive to be a protector and guardian of faith, family, and community, just as God and His angels protect and care for us.

historical_references.context: Waliha bint Al-Asqa'i, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, was named so due to her piety and dedication to the faith.
